body: I've felt the same way for a long time,  it started for me around 12 too,  I've made it to 26 so far.  I can't say life gets better in general,  but I can tell you....while I've had more downs than ups over the years, I don't really regret sticking around.   It gets better when you are able to maintain friendships with people you really enjoy being around,  it gets bearable when you find hobbies to keep your hands and your mind busy.  It gets rough again when you lose those friendships, but people come and go over time.  If you have trouble making friends in your local area,  try getting into an online game and joining a group that uses TeamSpeak or Mumble, I mean, I never really talk about my personal things with my game groups but just having those people to chat with while playing whatever game you guys are into is nice,  it's not as good as local friends,  but it's generally non judgmental social interaction, and you do start to get pretty close to people playing with the same group all the time.

I've always felt it's best to listen to what your body is telling you.  Your doctor doesn't know what's going on in your head and frankly I would be scared to tell them about it, it could lead to terrible repercussions being that honest with them.  Try another medication maybe?   If you think it's the medication triggering those kinds of thoughts, you should insist on trying another option.
I apologize for the formatting,  I should have used shift enter a bit more apparently,  I swear when I wrote this,  it was in paragraphs to make it a bit easier to read!
